::: {#fig-sequences}

```{r}
#| label: sequences-alt
#| include: false
fig_alt <- paste(
  "Two panels of points plotted against the index n from 1 to 10.",
  "In the first, the terms 1 over n fall from 1 toward 0,",
  "getting closer together.",
  "In the second, the terms of (-1) to the n alternate between -1 and 1."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: sequences-plot
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt
n <- 1:10
sequence_labels <- c("a_n = 1/n", "b_n = (-1)^n")
sequences <- data.frame(
  n = rep(n, 2),
  sequence = factor(
    rep(sequence_labels, each = length(n)),
    levels = sequence_labels
  ),
  term = c(1 / n, (-1)^n)
)

sequences_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(sequences) +
  ggplot2::aes(x = n, y = term) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.5, colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~sequence, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = n) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Index, n", y = "Term value") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  htmltools::div(
    role = "img",
    `aria-label` = fig_alt,
    plotly::ggplotly(sequences_plot)
  )
} else {
  sequences_plot
}
```

The first ten [terms](#def-sequence-term) of the [sequences](#def-sequence) $a_n = 1/n$ and $b_n = (-1)^n$ of @exm-sequence, plotted against $n$.
The terms of $b_n$ take only two [values](#def-value).

:::
